test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 17 Dec, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: A dealer marks his goods at 29% above the cost price and allows a discount of 7% on the marked price. What is his gain or loss percentage?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net multiplier = (1 + 29%) × (1 − 7%)

= 1.29 × 0.93 = 1.1997

Gain = (1.1997 − 1) × 100 = 19.97%

**∴ Answer = 19.97% gain**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Marked price = 29% above cost price

Discount = 7%

**Formula used:**

SP = CP × (1 + mark%) × (1 − discount%)

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let CP = 100

⇒ MP = 100 × 1.29 = 129

⇒ SP = 129 × 0.93 = 119.97

⇒ Gain = 119.97 − 100 = 19.97

⇒ Gain% = 19.97%

**∴ The correct answer is 19.97% gain.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage

Net effect = (1 + a)(1 − b)

Profit Formula

Profit% = (SP − CP) ÷ CP × 100

Assumption Method

Assume CP = 100 for easy calculation

Key Insight

Always combine markup and discount multiplicatively
